correctness.rationale: Each coordinate has the form dot X=A-B(X); one-variable antiderivative generator tests give E[A|X]=B(X), and orthogonal projection gives Var(A)-Var(B)=E[dot X^2]. For PN, zero defect makes PN constant and k1 P2=k2 PN, hence P2 constant; the P2 equation and strict monotonicity of J3 force P1 constant, then J1 forces P0 constant, then the P0 equation forces M constant, giving equilibrium. For M, zero speed makes M constant and S(PN) constant; S is injective on nonnegative concentrations, so PN is constant and the same propagation applies. Non-equilibrium endpoint speeds therefore have positive second moments and, with zero mean, cross both signs. Variation of constants in dot PN+k2 PN=k1P2 along a bounded complete trajectory gives the exact exponential memory, and the fifth conditional law gives the instantaneous projection. The verifier correctly checks the abstract variance decomposition and nuclear scaling coefficients.
